archetype.name: Playoff Team (5-on-5 driven, special teams lagging)
archetype.definition: Ottawa wins the even-strength game well enough to be a solid playoff club, but its 15-6-3 start has been helped by close-game luck and one hot goalie, while a broken power play holds it back.

report.headline: Real 5-on-5 team, inflated standings: close-game luck masks a broken power play
report.take:
Ottawa is second in the Atlantic at 15-6-3, with 33 points from 24 games and an 82-game pace of 113 points. The site has it 16th of 32, which says the record is ahead of the team. Both views have something to them. The underlying play is legitimately good. A 5-on-5 xGF % of .551 ranks 5th, shot attempts lean their way (CF % .51, 8th), and only 25.5 shots against a game (8th) explains why goals allowed per game ranks 7th. This isn't new. Last season's xGF % was .556 and its Goal Diff / GP was 0.39, almost identical to this year's 0.38.

What has changed is the bounce of close games. Last year Ottawa banked 3.2 fewer points than its goal differential implied and finished with 99. This year it leads the league in Pts vs Goal Diff at +3.4. A Goal Diff / GP of 0.38 ranks only 10th, which is a good team, not a 113-point one. The recent run shows the pattern: 2-1 wins over Buffalo and Winnipeg, a 4-3 overtime win over Colorado, and three of the last six games past regulation. The 5-on-5 PDO of 102.7 adds a second layer of even-strength fortune on top.

The numbers also hide two things pulling in opposite directions. The first is the power play: 13.5%, dead last, against a league average of 22.5%. That is the main reason a top-five chance-share team scores at only a 14th-ranked rate. Ottawa ran a 24% power play last season, so this should recover, and that is real upside the standings don't yet reflect. The second is the crease split. Linus Ullmark is at .937 with +10.6 GSAx, 4th on the goalie tab. Samuel Ersson is at .869 and -6.7, 66th of 72. Together they average out to a C grade and a team GSAx of -2.6. Ottawa's points come much more readily with Ullmark in net than with Ersson.

The direction is still up in form: 7-1-2 over the last ten and 4-0-1 over the last five, with the margin widening to 1.2 goals a game. Expect the close-game luck to cool and the power play to warm up, which roughly cancels out. That leaves a team that should finish around last year's level, near 100 points and in the playoff picture, rather than at its current pace.

strengths.title: Wins the even-strength chance battle
strengths.body: An xGF % of .551 (5th) and only 25.5 shots against a game show a team that controls play at 5-on-5. It matches last season's .556 almost exactly, so this is a repeatable identity rather than a hot month. It is the foundation that keeps Ottawa a playoff-caliber team even when the bounces turn.

strengths.title: Ullmark is elite so far
strengths.body: Ullmark's .937 save % and +10.6 GSAx rank him 4th of 72 goalies on the site, with a 1.47 GAA over 12 starts. A .937 is unlikely to hold all year. Even so, behind a team that limits shots, an above-average Ullmark makes Ottawa very hard to beat. How many starts he gets is the single biggest lever on the season.

strengths.title: Form improving with real margin
strengths.body: The last five games went 4-0-1 at 3.8 goals for and 2.6 against, a differential 0.82 a game better than the season rate. Unlike some of the earlier one-goal wins, this stretch includes clear wins over Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. November's goals against also fell from October's rate.

concerns.title: Standings points outrunning goal differential
concerns.body: Ottawa leads the league in Pts vs Goal Diff at +3.4, while its Goal Diff / GP of 0.38 ranks only 10th. Last season the same metric was -3.2, which shows how quickly close-game luck flips. Expect the points pace to slide toward what a 10th-best differential supports.

concerns.title: League-worst power play
concerns.body: A 13.5% power play ranks 32nd, nine points below the league average. It is why a top-five play-driving team scores at a middling rate. Ottawa ran 24% last season and 23.8% the year before, so a strong rebound is likely, but until it comes the team leaves goals on the table every night.

concerns.title: The backup is sinking the goalie numbers
concerns.body: Ersson has made 8 starts with an .869 save % and -6.7 GSAx, which drags the team's goaltending to a C grade and a -2.6 team GSAx (22nd). Wingers and defensemen are also producing above expectation against Ottawa (ranks 26th and 23rd). Some of that is the crease, and some is coverage leaving the flanks open.

trend.note: After a 9-6 October that allowed three goals a game, Ottawa tightened up in November and has gone 7-1-2 over its last ten. Several of those results were one-goal or overtime games, though.

weekAhead.headline: Calgary at home, then a four-stop road trip through contenders
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with the softest game: Calgary at home. The Flames have a 30th-ranked Goal Diff / GP, the 31st-ranked offense and D- goaltending, and Ottawa should be favored. Then the trip turns hard. Florida suppresses shots (24.2 against a game, 4th) and kills penalties at 84.6%. Tampa is a point behind Ottawa in the division and has the 3rd-best xGF %. Carolina, the next night, is the site's No. 1 team with the league's best xGF % and goal differential. The trip ends in Nashville, whose goalies rank 6th in GSAx and whose kill ranks 2nd.

The Tampa and Carolina games fall on consecutive nights, which almost certainly puts Ersson in net for one of them. That matters a great deal given the gap between Ottawa's two goalies. Several of these opponents also have strong penalty kills, so the power-play slump probably won't break this week. Ottawa needs to win at 5-on-5, which is its strength. Taking five or six points from five games would be a good week; something like that is the realistic target.

keyMatchups.title: Carolina's suffocating forward defense
keyMatchups.body: Carolina allows forwards just 0.09 points a game, first in the league, behind a .606 xGF %. Ottawa's chance-share edge, its main weapon, will be tested hardest here. Coming on the second night of back-to-backs, this is the week's toughest game.

keyMatchups.title: Division showdown in Tampa
keyMatchups.body: Tampa sits at 15-6-2, effectively tied with Ottawa atop the Atlantic, and drives play even better (xGF % .566). Its 73.3% penalty kill ranks 23rd, though. That makes Tampa the most likely opponent for Ottawa's power play to finally cash in against.

keyMatchups.title: Special teams against Calgary and Nashville
keyMatchups.body: Calgary's 26.3% power play (5th) faces an Ottawa kill at 76.2%, the main way the Flames can steal the home game. Nashville's 89.1% kill is the worst possible matchup for a power play that ranks last.

weekAhead.watch: Which goalie starts in Tampa and in Carolina on consecutive nights: Ullmark's starts are worth far more than Ersson's right now.

restOfSeason.body:
The even-strength profile is durable. It matches last season almost to the decimal, so Ottawa should keep controlling play and stay comfortably in the playoff race. Two things should change from here. The league-best Pts vs Goal Diff will fade as close games even out, and the last-place power play should climb toward the low-20s it ran in each of the past two seasons. Those roughly offset, which points to a final line close to last year's 99 points rather than the current 113-point pace. My range is 98 to 106 points and 45 to 49 wins.

The ceiling depends on the crease. If Ullmark keeps carrying most starts at an above-average level and Ersson recovers even toward average, the goaltending grade climbs and Ottawa can push the top of that range and contend for the division. If Ersson's numbers hold and Ullmark cools from .937, the team's modest goal differential leaves little margin, and the Atlantic is crowded enough that a wild-card spot becomes the realistic outcome.
swingFactors: Ullmark's share of starts and whether his .937 holds up
How fast the power play recovers toward last year's level
Close-game luck reverting from the league's best mark

confidence.note: 24 games is enough for the chance-share numbers to mean something; the goalie and power-play splits are still small samples.
